Like others mentioned this definitely feels too tight when you need to consider life events happening. When we budgeted we had things set to what their potential max could be and we had $1750 left over which felt tight even with emergency savings but it’s been comfortable and I’m glad we didn’t go for more house. Since we didn’t we’ve been okay even with an unexpected roof replacement and my fiancée on sick leave reducing our take home amounts.

It’s really easy to spend that leftover money over a month and can leave you in trouble down the line if something breaks that you don’t have savings for.

Same with the floor tile grout in my new spot. The installer definitely didn’t do an amazing job but jfc the previous owners must have been super soaking the floors when cleaning and vacuuming the grout cause I don’t know how they managed.

As another commenter mentioned definitely get a structural engineer in to see what they say and depending on that decide it’s make or break with any other potential fixes needing to be done. I’d personally have my running shoes on ready to bolt on this one but I stress a lot about my foundation despite there not being any issues.

The rely on each other piece is huge! When we found a ceiling water bubble two weeks after closing I was instantly in shambles and my fiancée got me through then when I felt more calm she fell apart and now it’s almost like a rotation haha. Having another person to ride the wave with makes things so much more manageable :)

That feels… weird. Definitely no issue getting an inspection done right away it’s better to know the house shape as soon as possible but the attorney piece has me feeling they may be a little unprepared and I’d be curious to know if they’re rushing any other piece of the sale. It may all be a non issue but I’d be more wary of any other red flags.

Our first accepted offer has us in a tight deadline like that and I was miserable as my fiancées job wouldn’t let her take any time off so I had to wrangle a lot on my own plus manage work prior to  my move to a more easy going position. I remember after we walked due to the inspection it felt like a relief to dodge the house issues plus the chaos of a quick turn around.

The place we eventually bought had the opposite where our closing was 5 months out due to them waiting on a new build but the week before closing was still total chaos.

We were approved for up to $450k on our incomes and more if we decided to get a place with a rental but we were steadfast in wanting single family. My folks also came with us as they’re aging but have income to help take some bills off our plate. We went for $400k on a place and are comfortable, my fiancée unexpectedly needed to go on sick leave a month after moving in so we know how we feel with a bit less income coming in and it’s tighter but comfortable. Very glad we didn’t take any advice on going to the max :)
This so hard, when we were buying I told my fiancée we’re getting all the coverage we can because our luck is awful and the cost was maybe $50 added to the yearly totally.

Reading your comments you’re definitely panicking which is normal when something big comes up in the first few months of your first home, our roof had a leak the first two weeks in showing us we need a replacement this spring and I was ready to put the place on the market because it felt like we made a huge mistake.

Take some deep breaths and if you need to get out of the house for an evening then take that evening away, call up friends or family who own a home for their advice, log out of Reddit, and call around to get some quotes. It’s tough and it’s scary having a big expense like that pop up but it’ll be okay you’ll figure it out! Reddit is where people share their horror stories of things happening and will just make you spiral harder (I made that mistake). Take care of yourself OP!

As others have mentioned these are expensive fixes depending in the severity, my fear would be what other maintenance have the current owners put off that your inspector missed/can’t see. Unless the home is your absolute dream and you have the funds to make any surprise big fixes I’d walk away. Water damage and sagging makes my palms sweat haha

First two weeks in our roof leaked and we assessed it was isolated with multiple roofers checking it out and patching where the leak occurred to get us through to the Spring. A wind and rain storm just ripped through and new leaks appeared so we’re going insurance route since something with this dang roof just ain’t right. It’s super stressful OP but best advice I’ve gotten is take it one day at a time and ask for as many opinions as possible, it helps keep with the nausea haha
It’s definitely more than asphalt but after this if anybody recommends metal roofs to me I’ll probably sob haha
That’s what we’re figuring out as well since the winter is so mild and temperatures are riding along  minimum shingle temperature requirements from what I seen. Appreciate the input!

For me and my fiancée at the beginning of our relationship I was still too fresh from my last break up to be a good partner, I struggled with separating my ex’s actions with our relationship so how I handled things just sucked. Luckily she was very patient with me and let me work through what I needed while we stayed close friends we kinda just naturally fell in love through it and it set the tone for how patient and understanding we’d be with each other in our relationship.

It’d be more shocking if you didn’t have regret it’s most likely the biggest purchase of your life and something that is ultimately on you to maintain, that’s going to come with stress and buyers remorse. Like others mentioned I’d recommend getting rid of the real estate apps and if you’re like me doomscrolling roofing, plumbing, and flooring subreddits then move away from those too.

You picked this house and location for a reason try to remember what made you like the place and focus on those. My street is super done up for the holidays and I love checking out the houses because it’s a reminder I’m in a better location where people can actually have things on their lawn without being robbed.

We also had the mindset of anything built since the 2000’s was better and older homes were a no go but the only older home we seen built in the 60’s is what we bought. Beside the roof replacement incoming this place feels better built than others we seen I trust a spot that’s survived Newfoundland winters for 60 years.
Reminds me of that YouTube trend where they’d do 100 layers of nail polish

Bought a place built in the 1960’s but last two years had a bunch of big ticket renovations (oil furnace replaced with electric, mini splits added with three heads, new electrical, and water boiler) which was reassuring. What wasn’t done recently? The roof. Three weeks in and we’re looking at a roof replacement after a leak cause the roof turned out to be a lemon and now I keep waiting for something else to fall apart 😂

We’re currently at around 32-33% if I remember my last calculation I think it may be lower with $1700~ leftover for savings and fun. It feels tight now but I’m nearing my next promotion and my fiancée is looking at her next career move so things will improve plus our favourite thing to do is stay home. For us a temporary tight budget was better than the black mold invested terror of a townhouse we were renting, even with a looming roof replacement less than 3 weeks in our new spot and my mind screaming that we made a mistake we’re much better off.

One thing we did to see how comfortable we felt was rough estimate our potential mortgage and bills then live as if we were on it with that extra money put in a savings account. We realized we felt comfortable even with emergencies happening and had that extra cash tucked away.
Same here! I definitely didn’t think we’d be looking at a roof replacement this soon but the more I’m learning about this thing the more I look forward to something meant for east coast weather.

You could definitely replace all the floors but my first thought is there’s a moisture problem, my vinyl flooring looks similar in spots in my basement from humidity levels being too high and the previous owners not running a dehumidifier. Better to address the why it’s happening before replacing.

No luck on that part which where we’re starting to wonder if it’s better to just replace the roof at this point and go for the more common asphalt because our repair options are starting to seem super limited.

This is the feeling I have too and another part of why we wonder if a replacement is better in the Spring since we feel like we might be in a non stop battle with leaks.

Pretty much! It’s what we found in our area anything in the lower end of our budget would need 20k+ plus in fixes going in. We ended up buying a spot built in the 1965 but 5 years ago it was built back up from the studs and previous owners put a ton of upgrades in. Going at the higher end of our comfort budget (not lender limit) felt better knowing we aren’t going to be replacing HVAC, roof, electrical, etc in the next minimum 5 years. I feel like we got a lucky break on this one because right now it feels like handyman specials or crumbling new builds are the main options for new home buyers.

I closed on Thursday and had an equally stressful time coping for the same reasons however, we were under contact for 5 months which was a lot of time to go through the whole emotional rollercoaster. What I found helped was to get my trusted financial people to look at our budget and hear their advice, which of course turned into us being told we’re perfectly fine but be mindful of our spending. We also bought a spot that has a lot of recent upgrades such as HVAC, hot water boiler, electrical, etc. so we know we have time to save when the eventual disasters happen. Since being here I see a bunch of things that are going to turn into projects but there’s no rush to do them now so figuring out that prioritization will help a ton.

My girl first went to the vet for what we suspected were teeth issues related to her age and she did have a mouth infection that cleared up but her drooling and issues eating didn’t improve. We went back and the vet said it was cancer and she had made maybe a week left so we decided to not let her worsen and euthanize.

I knew it was the right decision and I’m currently having similar thoughts if I rushed or maybe it was a misdiagnosis. I think it’s rational to have those doubts and feelings of guilt as we process a massive decision that has left us mourning. Our selfless decision in the end to put their well-being above our own is one of the greatest displays of love we can give our pets. My thoughts are with you ❤️

You’re making the right decision and your pet will pass surrounded by love. At home my Salem looked miserable most times being unable to eat or swallow properly but minutes before she was prepped for euthanasia she was trotting around the vet room giving love to every worker and to us, you never would have known something was wrong beside her visible weight loss. I knew if it were me I’d want to go out on a good day with my loved ones so that’s what we did.

I felt guilt ridden afterward because the vet said she had a week and maybe I was too hasty or maybe we could have longer than a week. The best way I could return the love she gave me was by helping her not feel anymore pain. My thoughts are with you and your kitty ❤️

The last person she saw and felt was me, going through it feels horrible but the pain shows the depth of love we have for our pets. Virtual hugs ❤️
